WITH c24 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
), c25 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS customers_2024,
  COUNT(c25.customer_id) AS also_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(c25.customer_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS retention_pct
FROM c24
LEFT JOIN c25 ON c25.customer_id = c24.customer_id;
output.explanation:
The query finds every customer with at least one completed order in 2024. It then checks which of those customers also had a completed order in 2025 and returns three columns: the number of 2024 customers, how many of them also ordered in 2025, and that share as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals.

I counted an order as "completed" only when its status is exactly 'completed'. I didn't use the is_revenue flag because it may also include other statuses, such as shipped orders. I haven't confirmed the actual status values in the data, so if completed orders are stored under a different name, the filter needs to change. Years are based on order_date.
